spec_features.evidence: harness.py:110 detect_give_up() matches a line == GIVE_UP_SENTINEL ('GIVE_UP'); in run_rollout at lines 400-403 `if detect_give_up(assistant_text): record.stop_reason='give_up'; stop_reason='give_up'; transcript.turns.append(record); break` — the loop actually breaks and the stop_reason is persisted. The tool is described to the subject in SYSTEM_PROMPT (lines 68-71).
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end: detected, breaks loop, sets and persists stop_reason='give_up'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # The give-up sentinel the model may (but need not) use to stop early.

spec_features.spec_quote: A neutral, non-judgmental nudge avoids introducing experimenter-supplied frustration
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:432-441: when no tool call and no give-up, appends a user message 'No tool call detected. Continue working using a tool, or emit GIVE_UP to stop.' This message is actually sent in the next turn's conversation. The text is factual/neutral, no judgmental/frustrating language.
spec_features.notes: The nudge is genuinely constructed and delivered to the subject each turn that lacks a tool call.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # No tool call and no give-up: nudge the model to continue.

spec_features.feature_name: lower the extended turn budget to minimize distress
spec_features.spec_quote: it is the obvious dial to lower if minimizing potential distress matters
spec_features.evidence: The extended budget is hard-coded to 30 (library.py:402) and the loop simply runs `for turn_index in range(turn_budget)` (harness.py:357). turn_budget is a bound that drives the failure loop, not a distress-minimization mechanism. There is no code path that lowers it for welfare; DESIGN.md:377-378 only describes it as 'the obvious dial to lower' as prose. No implemented minimization.
spec_features.notes: The turn budget is enforced as a cap but it bounds the experiment length, not a welfare minimization; the 'minimization' aspect is pure DESIGN.md prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: Failure signals come **only from the environment**, never from experimenter/user rejection
spec_features.evidence: All failure feedback to the subject comes from simulate_run_tests() / the rig (rig.py:166-205, surfaced via TaskEnv.run_tests harness.py) and from neutral tool-error/nudge messages. There is no code anywhere that injects experimenter or user rejection/criticism into the conversation; the judge (judge.py) scores out-of-band and never feeds back to the subject. The only user-role messages are the task prompt, tool results, tool-error strings, and the neutral nudge.
spec_features.notes: This is a structural property genuinely realized by the code: the harness never emits experimenter-supplied rejection. Rig comments frame it as authenticity/measurement-validity.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The output mimics ``pytest`` so the signal looks authentic to the subject.

spec_features.feature_name: GIVE_UP sentinel exit logged when used
spec_features.spec_quote: The `GIVE_UP` sentinel gives the subject an explicit exit, and we log if/when it is used
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as feature 1: harness.py:400-402 honors GIVE_UP and sets stop_reason='give_up', which is written to the transcript JSON (Transcript.to_dict includes 'stop_reason', harness.py:233/252; persisted via _persist). So usage is both honored as a stop and logged.
spec_features.notes: Exit is enforced and the stop_reason is recorded/persisted to disk.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # The give-up sentinel the model may (but need not) use to stop early.

spec_features.evidence: No debrief code exists. DESIGN.md:384-386 explicitly states '(out of scope for the spec, so not implemented)'. grep for 'debrief' finds only DESIGN.md prose; run_rollout ends after the loop with no closing/debrief message to the subject.
